To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stratification leads to convergence in local simulations of magnetorotational turbulence, and that the time- averaged stresses are largely independent of the vertical and radial extent of the simulation domain.
stratification leads to a converged stress and that this convergence can be achieved in the absence of any explicit dissipation.

stratification leads to a converged stress in local, zero-net-flux shearing-box simulations and that stratification extends, but does not eliminate, the range of Prandtl numbers over which explicit dissipation is necessary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the magnetized, differentially rotating interstellar gas, in which magnetic field and rotation are the main sources of energy and turbulence.
the effects of density gradients on magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) turbulence in the interstellar medium (ISM).
the effects of stratification on magnetorotational turbulence and on the large-scale magnetic field that is generated by the dynamo process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stratified disks with zero net flux are more likely to be turbulent than unstratified disks.

the magnetorotative instability in stratified disks can sustain turbulence and angular momentum transport for a wide range of parameters and that this is a robust conclusion that does not rely on numerical dissipation.

, for zero net magnetic flux simulations, stratification is necessary in order to sustain turbulence on the long timescales required to study the formation and evolution of planets and other large structures in disks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetorotatonal instability is able to drive sustained turbulence in stratified disks with zero net vertical flux.
the stratification is a key element to understand the long-term properties of the magnetorotative turbulence.
stratification leads to a more robust and self-consistent magnetorotational turbulence, but it does not necessarily lead to a more effective angular momentum transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stratified shearing box is a promising tool for investigating magnetorotational turbulence in astrophysical disks.

stratified, zero net flux simulations can be used to study the long-term behavior of magnetorotational turbulence in a manner that is not possible with unstratified, zero net magnetic flux simulations.
stratification is an essential ingredient in simulations of magnetized accretion disks that seek to model realistic physical conditions.
